bug_semantics: In v5.5.16, an authenticated victim can be sent to bbs/member_confirm.php?url=\attacker.example. bbs/member_confirm.php accepts that request-controlled $url, and check_url_host() parses only a copy with backslashes removed; the copy looks like a relative path and has no foreign host, while the original leading backslash survives the endpoint's incomplete /^\/\\/ and /^\/{3,}/ normalization. skin/member/basic/member_confirm.skin.php then emits the surviving value as the password-confirmation form action. Browser URL normalization can treat the backslash form as an external destination, so submitting the form redirects/posts the victim's mb_id and mb_password to an attacker-controlled origin.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable data-to-form-action mechanism first appears in reachable source history at a4b2e70e4d68d7cadad58f170b47aef36ae4fbe5: the new member-confirmation skin assigns the request-derived $url to f.action during submit without a host allowlist. fd92af89ec6d9822397184f3f20e9eb0b9b86336 later refactored the same sink into a direct <form action="<?php echo $url ?>"> without changing trust semantics. The 974-file GnuBoard5 import 41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b is not the BIC: its two relevant files are an exact G4-to-G5-name conversion of the reconstructable source-lineage state (the relevant trees at 0f78b67eb7ea7ecf72a3f24c0624d11349f7daec and 41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b are identical).

reasoning: The advisory-first trace establishes a credential-bearing open-redirect/form-action flaw in v5.5.16: host validation operates on a backslash-stripped parsing copy, while the original request value reaches the password form. The first patch that breaks that path is e03e01d41098f6a42788e53cb8bd5894ce47cd15, which removes backslashes before the endpoint emits the action; it lands after v5.5.16 and is contained by the vendor's v5.5.17 boundary at 8c505f6f1da4a8a63b32e9c6d1fa906e738cb4d2. For origin, the giant 41d21074b5fcf579633c255f3b499434b2d4d46b import cannot be treated as the BIC. Reconstructable parallel source history shows the same flow originating in a4b2e70e4d68d7cadad58f170b47aef36ae4fbe5 as an unvalidated JavaScript-assigned action, changing presentation but not trust semantics at fd92af89ec6d9822397184f3f20e9eb0b9b86336, and reaching a relevant tree identical to the GnuBoard5 aggregate at 0f78b67eb7ea7ecf72a3f24c0624d11349f7daec. Both vulnerable paths are absent from a4b2e70e4d68d7cadad58f170b47aef36ae4fbe5's direct parent. Finally, the raw BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI authorship/co-authorship marker, so BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI.
